newsitem.title: USA: NRC staff paves way for Salem N.J. 2 nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: NRC staff paves way for Salem N.J. 2 nuke restart.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday its staff recommended to senior officials that they approve restart one of the two idled nuclear units at the Salem nuclear power plant in New Jersey.
"The team says it's (Salem unit 2) is ready for restart," a NRC spokeswoman said.
A 14-person NRC inspection team combed through the facility for two weeks earlier this month, and reviewed improvements performed on the unit over past two years.
The regional NRC administrator must give his authorization before the reactor could be reactivated, she said.
The operator, Public Service Electric and Gas Co (PSE&G) must also send a letter to the NRC admininstrator stating that the unit can be operated safely, she added.
The two Salem units, each rated at 1,106 megawatts, have been shut since mid-1995 after NRC raised concerns over the units' safety.
The NRC team and PSE&G discussed the findings on Salem 2 last Friday.
PSE&G earlier said it hopes the Salem 2 would be putting power back on the grid in late July following two to three weeks of low power testing.
The company has aimed to restore Salem 1 to service in autumn.
In addition to PSE&G, owners of Salem are PECO Energy Co, Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Inc.
